title: Lock-off Training
texts: 3 sets of lock-off practice on vertical or slightly overhanging terrain

Find an area in the gym with a large hand hold on vertical to slightly overhanging terrain and various hold options.  Start with both hands matched on the starting hold and feet placed anywhere.  Move your left hand to the first hold, and while still keeping your right hand on the starting hold, bump to the next hold.  Repeat this process 2 more times for a total of 4 hand movements with your left hand.  Your right hand should remain on the original starting hold.  Switch hands and repeat with your right hand as the bumping hand.  Each hand move should get progressively harder.  You will need to experiment with various foot options to maximize the distance you can bump with your leading hand.  You should find that high feet are the most rewarding regarding the maximum distance reached.

Complete this process on 2 additional boulders.  You will complete 3 climbs, with 4 hand movements on each side (each side counts as 1 rep), for a total of 24 hand moves.  More experienced climbers may complete this workout on a spray wall or on steeper wall angles.  

If you have a history of elbow tendonitis, such as golfer’s elbow, we recommend skipping or exercising caution with this workout.  In particular, deep lock-offs (acute elbow angles) should be avoided, and instead, work on wide lock-offs where more emphasis is placed on shifting your weight over the leading foot and keeping a wider elbow angle.
